## Preface

The primary goal of Open Source Football is to make football analysis and the
code behind it publicly available. To achieve this, we need volunteers who are
willing to contribute.

Posts are written with [Quarto](https://quarto.org). You can write in **R, Python,
or both**. Any language Quarto supports works, as long as your post can be rendered
locally.

If you have questions or think something is unclear or wrong, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/nflverse/open-source-football/issues/new).

## Overview

1. Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and git.
2. Fork the repository and clone it.
3. Create a new branch.
4. Copy the post template to `posts/YYYY-MM-DD-short-title/` and write your post.
5. Render your post locally. This executes your code once and stores the
   results in `_freeze/`.
6. Commit your post folder **and** its `_freeze/` folder, then open a pull request.

We will review the post, suggest changes if necessary, and publish it by merging
the pull request.

## Detailed instructions

### Set up

You need [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) (≥ 1.5), git, and
whatever language you write in. For R posts, install `rmarkdown` and `knitr`.
For Python posts, install `jupyter`.

The [usethis pull request helpers](https://usethis.r-lib.org/articles/pr-functions.html)
make forking and branching easy from R:

```r
usethis::create_from_github("nflverse/open-source-football")
usethis::pr_init(branch = "my-post-title")
```

Using plain git or the GitHub CLI works just as well:

```sh
gh repo fork nflverse/open-source-football --clone
cd open-source-football
git switch -c my-post-title
```

### Create the post

Copy the template folder and give it a date-prefixed, descriptive name:

```sh
cp -r _post_template posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title
```

Open `posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title/index.qmd` and fill in the metadata (title,
description, author, date, categories). Then write your post.

A few conventions:

- **Load data so readers can rerun your code.** Use
  [nflreadr](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com) or
  [nflreadpy](https://github.com/nflverse/nflreadpy) rather than local files.
  Please don't commit large data files. If you must ship data, keep it small.
- Use `#| column: page` on chunks with wide figures or tables.
- Set `image:` in the metadata to choose the preview picture on the home page.
- For Python-only posts, add `jupyter: python3` to the metadata.

### Render and preview

```sh
quarto preview posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title/index.qmd
```

This runs your code and opens a live preview. When you're happy, render once more:

```sh
quarto render posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title/index.qmd
```

The site is configured with `freeze: true`, which means **your code is only ever
executed on your machine**. Rendering writes the results to
`_freeze/posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title/`. The website build reuses these frozen
results and never re-runs your code, so your post keeps working even if the data
or packages change later.

### Commit and open a pull request

Commit everything in your post folder **and** the matching `_freeze/` folder:

```sh
git add posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title _freeze/posts/2026-01-15-my-post-title
git commit -m "Add post: My post title"
```

Then push and open a pull request:

```r
usethis::pr_push()
```

or

```sh
git push -u origin my-post-title
gh pr create
```

Don't commit the `_site/` folder; the website is built automatically after
merging. A check on your pull request renders the whole site to make sure
everything works.

That's it. Thanks for your contribution!
